verdict: Avoid new castings and forgings exposure in Coimbatore for now; the local order story is real but Tamil Nadu's demand signal is weak and energy costs are high, so only lend to machined-component, export-order-backed units with tight structure.
title: Coimbatore castings & forgings: a note to the credit manager
narrative: Almost 65% of castings sold out of Coimbatore are machined, so value addition is rising [2]. Cash sits in the melting-and-pouring cycle and then in the machining queue; the export share means part of the receivable book is in foreign currency and moves with shipping time.

## What has changed now
**The local order book is genuinely strong: Coimbatore foundries saw 20% growth in the last one year on orders across auto, farm equipment and general engineering [2].** But the state-level demand signal is weak: Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 9.3 pp slower [D]. Power is not the constraint, with Tamil Nadu electricity demand +9.8% Apr-to-date against India +9.5% [D]. The cost side is the problem: Brent at $113/bbl is above the $75–100 band [D], and melting is energy-intensive, so when a proposal lands, check the power-and-fuel clause in the customer contract and ask who absorbs a further rise. National casting output (IIP NIC 24) grew only +2.4% YoY [D], so the Coimbatore growth is share gain, not a rising tide.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue the machined-component supplier with a named export or Tier-1 order, not the plain job-work pourer.** Peer results show where the money is: Ramkrishna Forgings grew revenue 54.9% YoY to ₹1,405 crore in Q2 FY27 with EBITDA margin at 18.23% and ₹673 crore of new orders [6]; Happy Forgings carries a ₹950 crore order book to be executed over 2-3 years, about 60% export [5], and posted Q4 FY26 revenue up 20.4% on 20.6% volume growth [7]. Avoid the commercial-vehicle-only supplier: Nelcast's revenue fell to ₹335 crore in Q2FY25 from ₹362.6 crore on subdued domestic and export CV demand [4]. Rating reports show the safe shape: gearing close to nil and TOL/TNW at 0.3 times [8], and margins improving to 8.4% OPM in FY2025 from 7.5% on softer raw material [11].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the order book, not the balance sheet.** Take assignment of export receivables or a charge on the specific order, keep the drawing power tied to machined dispatches, and insist on a promoter guarantee where gearing is above the peer norm. Every month take stock-and-receivable statements, the order-book position with customer names, power bills, and GST returns; if GST turnover trails the stock statement, ask for the dispatch register. Where the customer is a single Tier-1 buyer, cap exposure at a share of that buyer's payables. Collect from customer the split of export versus domestic sales and the currency of export billing before pricing.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the receivable days and the power bill together.** If receivable days stretch while power consumption per tonne rises, the unit is buying volume with working capital; stop enhancement and re-price. If export orders shift to a buyer in a new market, ask for the letter of credit before disbursing. If the promoter's other group entities draw on the same cash, treat it as a red flag. Note that the Coimbatore-specific sources are thin and partly promotional [1][3], so lean on the peer and rating evidence above.
